candidate.answerReason: The restrictions force b and c to be the endpoints. The only valid orders are bdac and cadb.

methods.label: Find the forced endpoints
methods.explanation:
Look first at the letters with the fewest possible neighbors. The letter \(b\) cannot be beside \(a\) or \(c\), so its only possible neighbor is \(d\). An interior letter would have two distinct neighbors, so \(b\) must be at an endpoint. Likewise, \(c\) can only be beside \(a\), so \(c\) must occupy the other endpoint.

If \(b\) comes first, its neighbor must be \(d\), and the neighbor of the final \(c\) must be \(a\). This forces \(bdac\). If \(c\) comes first, the same restrictions force \(cadb\).

Both orders satisfy the condition. Every valid order must have one of these two endpoint orientations, and each orientation forces exactly one order. Thus there are \(\boxed{2}\) rearrangements, choice \(\text{C}\).
